items.text: ALTMAN: WORLD SHOULD ACCEPT SOME AI RISKS OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says “the world should accept some bad things happening” to keep AI broadly accessible, arguing that people will ultimately use the technology for far more good than harm. Altman drew the line at catastrophic risks such as severe loss of control, while arguing that no single AI lab should control the technology.

OPENAI INTRODUCES NEW VISUAL ADS IN CHATGPT OpenAI is introducing a new visual advertising format in ChatGPT, with U.S. testing beginning later this month among an initial group of advertisers. The format will initially appear during image generation. OpenAI is also partnering with Haus, Measured and WorkMagic on ad-effectiveness experiments, while working with DoubleVerify and Integral Ad Science on brand-suitability testing.

COIN - BOFA RAISES COINBASE TARGET TO $203 BofA raised its Coinbase price target to $203 from $174, reiterating a Buy rating. The bank lifted its 2027–2028 EPS forecasts on expectations for stronger stablecoin revenue following September’s Fed hike. However, near-term estimates were trimmed as crypto trading volumes weakened despite Bitcoin and Ethereum rallying 43% and 70% in Q3.

BITCOIN RALLY REVIVES “DEBASEMENT TRADE” Bitcoin’s rally toward $86,000 reflects renewed demand for an anti-fiat hedge, according to Capital. com’s Kyle Rodda. Rodda links the move to Scott Bessent’s intervention in Treasury markets, arguing Bitcoin is increasingly trading as a hedge against expansive U.S. policy and a portfolio diversifier. He says the outlook is improving and the cycle lows may have already passed.

JPMORGAN: BOND YIELD SPIKE WON’T DERAIL STOCKS JPMorgan says the recent surge in bond yields should not cause lasting damage to equities, expecting yields to retreat from current highs. Strategist Mislav Matejka sees resilient economic growth and strong corporate earnings supporting stocks, while arguing inflation should remain contained. JPMorgan also believes much of the French political risk is already priced into the CAC 40.

BOFA: ACTIVE FUNDS STRUGGLE AS MEGACAPS DOMINATE Just 44% of large-cap active funds beat their benchmarks in September, as market leadership narrowed sharply toward megacaps, according to BofA. The cap-weighted S&P 500 outperformed its equal-weight counterpart by nearly 5 percentage points. Growth managers struggled most, with Meta and AMD accounting for 70% of the Russell 1000 Growth’s monthly gain.

IRGC THREATENS TANKER IN STRAIT OF HORMUZ UKMTO says a tanker transiting the Strait of Hormuz was hailed by Iran’s IRGC and instructed to turn back or risk being targeted. The tanker complied with the order. The incident was reported 11 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, adding to renewed concerns over shipping security through the key oil transit route.

TRUMP PLANS EXECUTIVE ACTION TO LOWER DIESEL COSTS President Trump plans executive actions Monday aimed at reducing diesel prices, including a Treasury review of certain diesel taxes and measures to expand access to tax-exempt dyed diesel, according to Politico. U.S. diesel averaged $6.32 a gallon Monday, down 13 cents from last week but still $2.63 higher than a year ago. Trump has ruled out a diesel export ban.

TRUMP: REFINERY DISRUPTIONS NOW DRIVING GASOLINE PRICES Trump says the Strait of Hormuz is no longer the main factor pushing gasoline prices higher, citing increased oil flows through the waterway. He instead points to refinery disruptions, including Ukrainian attacks on Russian facilities and refinery closures in U.S. Democratic-led states such as California.

Contacts are under medical observation and a local hospital has been quarantined. SAUDI ARABIA, PAKISTAN, TURKEY AGREE RAPID MILITARY DEPLOYMENT Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey convened an emergency meeting of the Mecca Alliance’s defense committee, Pakistan’s Foreign Ministry says. The three countries agreed to provide military forces and capabilities for rapid deployment in Saudi Arabia and condemned the attempted targeting of Mecca and Madinah. Pakistan’s Nauman Mahmood was named the alliance’s first secretary-general for a three-year term.

BESSENT: U.S. PRESSURE CAMPAIGN IS HITTING IRAN’S ECONOMY Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says “Operation Economic Outcast” is delivering results, pointing to a record-low Iranian rial and claiming Iran loaded zero crude onto tankers last month. Bessent says the campaign will continue until Tehran stops funding terrorism and pursuing a nuclear weapon.

AI OPTIMISM OVERRIDES RISING BOND YIELDS Tech stocks are rallying even as bond yields climb, with investors continuing to bet heavily on the long-term benefits of AI. Interactive Brokers strategist Steve Sosnick summed up the mood: “If you think the benefits of AI are essentially infinite, so what if you have to pay more to borrow money?”

SPCX - SPACEX PROPOSES 32-MILE GAS PIPELINE FOR STARSHIP SpaceX is seeking approval to build a 32.4-mile natural gas pipeline in Florida to supply methane for Starship launches from Cape Canaveral. The pipeline would connect with Florida Gas Transmission, replacing reliance on trucked LNG deliveries with a continuous gas supply as SpaceX expands launch operations. The company would still need infrastructure to liquefy the natural gas into rocket fuel.

HIGH YIELDS FORCE MUNI BORROWERS TO DELAY REFINANCINGS Roughly $6 billion of municipal bond refinancing deals are on hold or delayed as elevated yields erase potential savings for borrowers. Benchmark 30-year muni yields recently hit 5.26%, the highest since at least 2011. New Jersey postponed a planned $1.7 billion refunding, while Philadelphia delayed a $450 million deal. New York’s MTA is also considering a $1 billion refinancing, subject to market conditions.

TREASURY YIELDS SURGE TO FRESH 24-YEAR HIGHS Treasuries sold off sharply, pushing the 10-year yield to 5.34% and the 30-year to 5.70%, their highest levels since 2002. Pressure comes from resilient growth, AI-driven investment and persistent inflation, with ISM Services Prices Paid hitting 74.0, the highest since July 2022. Markets price roughly a 25% chance of an October Fed hike, with a full 25bp increase priced by December.

DALIO WARNS CHINA AND JAPAN COULD PULL BACK FROM TREASURIES Ray Dalio warns U.S. Treasuries are vulnerable to weakening demand from China and Japan, two of America’s largest foreign creditors. China’s holdings have fallen from $1.3 trillion in 2013 to about $618 billion, while Japan holds roughly $1.1 trillion. Dalio says reduced foreign demand could intensify pressure on U.S. borrowing as 10-year yields hover near 5.3%.

TSLA - GOLDMAN: TESLA’S AI STORY MATTERS MORE THAN Q3 EARNINGS Goldman Sachs reiterated its Neutral rating and $360 price target on Tesla ahead of Q3 earnings. The bank expects improving vehicle revenue from the Model Y L ramp, but says higher costs and capex could limit 2026 EPS upside. Goldman believes robotaxis, FSD and humanoid robots will matter more for Tesla’s stock reaction than Q3 earnings themselves.

JULIUS BAER SEES FINAL FED HIKE IN DECEMBER Julius Baer expects the Fed to deliver one final 25bp rate hike in December, followed by an extended pause. The bank points to a cooling U.S. labor market and sharply tighter financial conditions, driven more by rising long-term Treasury yields and a stronger dollar than by higher short-term rates. December is now seen as the most likely window for the final hike.

TRUMP SAYS U.S. WILL CONSIDER PERMANENT MILITARY BASE IN LITHUANIA President Trump says the U.S. will consider establishing a permanent military base in Lithuania, potentially replacing the current rotational model. Lithuania’s prime minister says the country is prepared to cover the costs of hosting a permanent U.S. presence. Around 1,000 U.S. troops have typically rotated through Lithuania, which has hosted American forces since 2014.

U.S. YIELDS RETREAT FROM 24-YEAR HIGHS Treasury yields pulled back as oil fell below $100 and Scott Bessent pledged that stronger growth and spending restraint would begin improving the U.S. debt trajectory. The 10-year yield fell to 5.27% and the 30-year to 5.63%, easing from levels last seen in 2002. Investors remain cautious, however, with the U.S. deficit near 6% of GDP and markets still pricing substantial Fed tightening.

But Hardy warns inventory buffers in the West are largely gone, and without these flows oil could face a $200-per-barrel scenario. S&P 500 ON TRACK FOR 28TH RECORD CLOSE OF 2026 The S&P 500 rose nearly 0.5% to around 7,810, putting it on course to surpass its Aug. 13 record closing high. The index is also approaching its 7,816.70 intraday record. A new high would mark the S&P 500’s 28th record close this year, while the Nasdaq is on track for a second consecutive record close.

U.S. GASOLINE AND DIESEL PRICES EASE, BUT REMAIN SHARPLY HIGHER U.S. regular gasoline fell slightly to $4.354 per gallon, but remains $1.23 higher than a year ago. Diesel saw a much larger weekly decline, falling 18.3 cents to $6.199 per gallon, yet remains $2.49 above year-ago levels. The Lower Atlantic recorded the largest declines, with gasoline falling 23.6 cents and diesel dropping 25.4 cents.

YELLEN BACKS RETALIATION AGAINST TRUMP TARIFFS Former Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen called President Trump’s treatment of U.S. allies “appalling” and said Canada and other countries should retaliate against protectionist measures rather than “accept this lying down.” Yellen argues tariffs have worsened affordability for Americans, while weakening cooperation with allies. Bloomberg Economics estimates the U.S. effective tariff rate at 11.2%, nearly 9 percentage points above early 2025 levels.

He argues the surge was driven largely by forced selling and intense competition for capital from AI investment and government borrowing, rather than inflation fears. TRUMP DIESEL TAX RELIEF CALLED A “BAND AID” U.S. diesel futures fell after President Trump temporarily allowed tax-deferred on-road use of red diesel through year-end, with the deferred federal excise tax potentially eliminated later. Ritterbusch says the measure may provide some relief but doesn’t address the underlying supply disruption through the Strait of Hormuz. Nymex diesel fell 2.6% to $4.4295 per gallon.

DRONE ATTACK SHUTS MAJOR RUSSIAN OIL REFINERY Russia’s Volgograd refinery completely halted crude processing on October 2 after equipment was damaged in a drone attack, industry sources told Reuters. The Lukoil-owned facility can process around 280,000 barrels per day, representing roughly 5% of Russia’s total refining capacity. The shutdown threatens to intensify Russia’s existing fuel crunch, as repeated attacks increasingly disrupt the country’s refining infrastructure.

BOJ’S SATO BACKS FURTHER RATE HIKES, BUT FLAGS WEAK CONSUMPTION BOJ board member Ayano Sato supports gradually raising interest rates, saying tighter policy can contribute to sustainable economic growth, but declined to specify the timing of the next hike. Sato, who opposed a rate hike at September’s meeting, said the decision reflected concern that consumer spending lacked momentum. DIMON WARNS AI HAS INCREASED CYBER RISK TENFOLD JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon says AI has increased cyber risk tenfold, making cybersecurity the bank’s biggest threat. He also warned governments “can’t borrow endlessly and spend endlessly,” as rising debt could push yields and credit spreads higher. On AI infrastructure, Dimon said companies should build data centers where communities want them, while arguing better policy could boost growth without additional spending.

EXPLOSION HEARD NEAR IRAN’S QESHM ISLAND The sound of an explosion was heard from the direction of the sea near Iran’s Qeshm Island, according to IRNA. No impact or strike has been reported on the island itself, and local sources have not yet provided further details. The cause of the explosion remains unclear.

U.S. POWER DEMAND TO HIT RECORD HIGHS ON AI BOOM U.S. electricity consumption is projected to reach record highs in both 2026 and 2027, driven partly by growing demand from AI and crypto data centers, according to the EIA. Power demand is expected to rise from 4,195 billion kWh in 2025 to 4,356 billion kWh in 2027. Renewables’ generation share is projected to reach 27% by 2027, while coal falls to 15%.
